newsitem.title: USA: Navistar to pay $11 million to clean up steel site.
newsitem.headline: Navistar to pay $11 million to clean up steel site.

text.p: Chicago-based Navistar International Transportation Corp. has agreed to pay $11 million to reimburse the federal government for its cleanup of Chicago's contaminated old Wisconsin Steel Works site.

Under the agreement, announced by the Justice Department late on Monday, Navistar will pay $5 million to the Commerce Department's Economic Development Administration for testing and cleanup work, as well as $5.95 million to settle claims on the foreclosure and ownership of the south Chicago site.
In addition, the company, a unit of Navistar International Corp., will assume full ownership and responsibility for the site, the Justice Department said.
Lois Shiffer, assistant Attorney General in charge of environment and natural resources, said the agreement would make the site suitable for future commercial use.
Commerce Department officials said the deal would spur economic development in Chicago's impoverished south side.

The steel mill site was owned and operated by Navistar since the late 19th century, but the site was sold to WSC Corp in 1977. In 1979, EDA agreed to guarantee 90 percent of $100 million in loans to WSC to upgrade the steel works, with Navistar backing the remaining 10 percent.
But WSC went bankrupt in 1980 and defaulted on the loans, and in 1981 EDA and Navistar purchased the site at a bankruptcy court sale.
